_meta.description: Troubleshooting missions for STM31733 Network Administration — 6 categories, 12 missions

missions.title: PC Cannot Ping the Default Gateway
missions.brief: A PC in the network is reporting no connectivity. The user cannot access any shared resources or the internet. Investigate and resolve the issue.
missions.fault: PC has incorrect default gateway configured (192.168.1.254 instead of 192.168.1.1)

steps.instruction: Run ipconfig on the PC and check the default gateway address
steps.hint: Open Command Prompt and type: ipconfig /all

steps.instruction: Ping the default gateway from the PC
Identify the incorrect gateway value and correct it
steps.hint: Change the PC gateway to match the router interface IP

missions.debrief: The PC was configured with the wrong default gateway (192.168.1.254 instead of 192.168.1.1). Always verify IP, mask and gateway with ipconfig /all as the first troubleshooting step.

missions.title: Layer 1 Connectivity Failure
missions.brief: Two routers that should be directly connected are unable to communicate. No routing protocols are converging.
missions.fault: Router interface is administratively shut down (no shutdown not applied)

steps.instruction: Check interface status on Router 1 using show ip interface brief
Identify the interface showing 'administratively down'
steps.hint: Look for 'administratively down' in the Status column

steps.instruction: Enter interface configuration mode and apply no shutdown
Verify connectivity with ping to the other router

missions.debrief: Cisco router interfaces are administratively down by default. Always verify interface status with 'show ip interface brief' before assuming a physical fault.

missions.title: VLAN Trunk Not Forming
missions.brief: Two switches are connected but VLANs are not propagating across the link. Devices on VLAN 10 on Switch 1 cannot communicate with devices on VLAN 10 on Switch 2.
missions.fault: Trunk port on SW1 is set to access mode, not trunk mode

steps.instruction: Check trunk status on SW1 using show interfaces trunk
Check the switchport mode on the connected port using show running-config
steps.hint: Look for 'switchport mode access' on the interswitch port

steps.instruction: Change the port mode to trunk with switchport mode trunk
Verify the trunk is now active with show interfaces trunk
steps.hint: The port should now appear in the trunk output

missions.debrief: Trunk ports must be explicitly configured on both sides. 'show interfaces trunk' quickly shows which ports are trunking and which VLANs are allowed.

missions.title: VLAN Missing from Database
missions.brief: Devices assigned to VLAN 20 cannot communicate with each other even though the port is correctly assigned. Verify the VLAN exists in the switch database.
missions.fault: VLAN 20 has not been created in the VLAN database (vlan.dat)

steps.instruction: List all VLANs with show vlan brief
Confirm VLAN 20 is not in the database
steps.hint: Look for VLAN 20 — it should not appear

steps.instruction: Create VLAN 20 and assign a name
Verify the VLAN appears and ports are assigned
steps.hint: show vlan brief — VLAN 20 should now show assigned ports

missions.debrief: A port assigned to a non-existent VLAN will not carry traffic. Always create the VLAN first, then assign ports.

missions.title: Static Route Pointing to Wrong Next-Hop
missions.brief: Users on the 192.168.10.0/24 network cannot reach the 192.168.30.0/24 network. A static route is configured but packets are being dropped.
missions.fault: Static route next-hop IP is incorrect — points to 192.168.20.3 instead of 192.168.20.2

steps.instruction: Run traceroute to 192.168.30.1 from the source router to see where packets drop
Check the routing table with show ip route on Router 1
steps.hint: show ip route — look for the 192.168.30.0 entry

steps.instruction: Identify the wrong next-hop in the static route
steps.hint: Compare the next-hop IP to the actual neighbour router interface IP

steps.instruction: Remove the incorrect route and add the correct static route

missions.debrief: Static routes fail silently when the next-hop IP is unreachable or wrong. Always verify next-hop reachability and check 'show ip route' carefully.

missions.title: RIPv2 Network Statement Missing
missions.brief: RIPv2 is configured on three routers but routes for the 192.168.40.0/24 network are not appearing in the routing table of Router 1.
missions.fault: Router 3 is missing the network statement for 192.168.40.0 in its RIP configuration

steps.instruction: Check RIP configuration on Router 3 using show running-config | section router rip
Identify the missing network statement
steps.hint: Compare network statements to Router 3's interface IPs

steps.instruction: Add the missing network statement under router rip
Verify routes appear on Router 1 with show ip route
steps.hint: Look for R 192.168.40.0 entries on Router 1

missions.debrief: RIPv2 only advertises networks explicitly listed with 'network' statements. A single missing statement can break end-to-end reachability.

missions.title: DHCP Pool Exhausted / Wrong Network
missions.brief: PCs on the network are receiving 169.254.x.x APIPA addresses instead of valid DHCP addresses. No devices can communicate.
missions.fault: DHCP pool is configured with wrong network address (192.168.2.0 instead of 192.168.1.0)

steps.instruction: Check DHCP pool configuration with show running-config | section dhcp
Compare the DHCP network to the router interface IP
steps.hint: DHCP network must match the connected interface subnet

steps.instruction: Delete the incorrect pool and recreate with the correct network
steps.hint: no ip dhcp pool POOL_NAME → recreate with correct network

steps.instruction: Release and renew DHCP on a PC and verify correct address assignment

missions.debrief: The DHCP network statement must exactly match the subnet of the connected interface. APIPA addresses always indicate DHCP failure.

missions.title: DNS Name Resolution Failing
missions.brief: Users can ping servers by IP address but cannot access them by hostname. Investigate the DNS configuration.
missions.fault: Router is missing the ip name-server statement pointing to the DNS server

steps.instruction: Test DNS resolution with nslookup on a client PC
Check DNS configuration on the router with show running-config
steps.hint: Look for ip name-server and ip domain-name in running-config

steps.instruction: Add the missing ip name-server statement on the router
Verify DNS resolution works from a client PC
steps.hint: nslookup server.local should now return an IP

missions.debrief: DNS requires both the server to be configured correctly and clients/routers to know the DNS server IP. 'ip name-server' tells the router where to send DNS queries.

missions.title: Telnet Still Enabled — Enable SSH
missions.brief: A security audit has flagged that VTY lines on the main router accept Telnet connections (plaintext). Configure SSH and disable Telnet access.
missions.fault: VTY lines configured with 'transport input all' instead of 'transport input ssh'

steps.instruction: Check VTY line configuration with show running-config | section line vty
Set a domain name required for RSA key generation
Generate RSA keys for SSH
Change VTY transport to SSH only
Verify SSH is working with show ip ssh
steps.hint: show ip ssh should show SSH Enabled

missions.debrief: Telnet transmits credentials in plaintext — always disable it and use SSH. Requires a domain name, RSA keys and 'transport input ssh' on VTY lines.

missions.title: Enable Password Not Encrypted
missions.brief: A router configuration has been reviewed and passwords are stored in plaintext in the running configuration. Secure the device passwords.
missions.fault: enable password used instead of enable secret; service password-encryption not applied

steps.instruction: View the running configuration and identify plaintext passwords
Replace enable password with enable secret
Apply service password-encryption globally
Verify passwords are now encrypted in running-config
steps.hint: show running-config — passwords should show as type 7 or type 5

missions.debrief: 'enable secret' uses MD5 hashing and is always preferred over 'enable password'. 'service password-encryption' encrypts other passwords (type 7) but is not highly secure — it prevents casual viewing.

missions.title: SNMP Community String Misconfigured
missions.brief: The network monitoring tool is not receiving SNMP data from the core router. Investigate and fix the SNMP configuration.
missions.fault: SNMP community string on the router does not match what the NMS is configured to use

steps.instruction: Check SNMP configuration with show running-config | section snmp
Identify the community string on the router
Compare to the NMS expected community string and correct the mismatch
steps.hint: NMS expects community string 'netadmin360' — update router to match

steps.instruction: Verify SNMP polling succeeds from the NMS
steps.hint: SNMP walk should return device OIDs

missions.debrief: SNMP community strings are case-sensitive passwords that must match exactly between the managed device and the NMS. Use SNMPv3 with authentication in production.

missions.title: Network Monitoring Report Analysis
missions.brief: You have been given a network monitoring report showing interface errors, high CPU utilisation and intermittent connectivity. Analyse the data and identify the root causes.
missions.fault: Multiple issues: duplex mismatch causing interface errors, high CPU due to routing loop, intermittent connectivity due to STP topology change

steps.instruction: Identify the interface showing the highest error count in the report
steps.hint: Look for input errors and CRC errors in the interface statistics

steps.instruction: Determine the likely cause of CRC/input errors
steps.hint: CRC errors with no physical damage usually indicate a duplex mismatch

steps.instruction: Identify the device showing abnormally high CPU (>80%) and explain why
steps.hint: A routing loop causes continuous packet forwarding — check for route with incrementing hop count

steps.instruction: Prepare a brief incident summary with root causes and recommended actions
steps.hint: Include: Issue, Root Cause, Impact, Recommendation for each finding

missions.debrief: Network monitoring reports provide early warning of issues before they become outages. Regular analysis and documentation is a key NOC skill.
